def _single_tensor_adamw(params, grads, exp_avgs, exp_avg_sqs, max_exp_avg_sqs, state_steps, *, amsgrad, beta1, beta2, lr, weight_decay, eps, maximize):
    for i, param in enumerate(params):
        grad = grads[i]
        exp_avg = exp_avgs[i]
        exp_avg_sq = exp_avg_sqs[i]
        step_t = state_steps[i]

        step_t.add_(1)
        step = step_t.item()

        # Perform stepweight decay
        param.mul_(1 - lr * weight_decay)

        if maximize:
            grad = -grad

        # Decay the first and second moment running average coefficient
        exp_avg.lerp_(grad, 1 - beta1)
        exp_avg_sq.mul_(beta2).addcmul_(grad, grad, value=1 - beta2)

        bias_correction1 = 1 - beta1 ** step
        bias_correction2 = 1 - beta2 ** step
        step_size = lr / bias_correction1
        bias_correction2_sqrt = math.sqrt(bias_correction2)

        denom = (exp_avg_sq.sqrt() / bias_correction2_sqrt).add_(eps)
        param.addcdiv_(exp_avg, denom, value=-step_size)

optimizer_semantics_probe.note: Measured on a throwaway parameter: the variant listed in 'measured_variant' is the one that reproduces this PyTorch build's update bit for bit.

notes: Round-trip check: the decoded sign/exponent/fraction re-encode to the observed raw word.
numpy and torch reinterpretation paths are compared against each other, so a systematic error in one would show up as a disagreement.
Real training: torch loss.backward() and optimizer.step() only. No gradient is assigned, no parameter value is written outside the optimizer, and no trajectory is precomputed.
The float64 track is a separate real run of the same forward shape in a different precision. It is a reference, not ground truth.
